Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

jnanalytics 0.1.0.9000

First version. jnanalytics succeeds hoaddata 0.3: it covers all journals in transformative agreements, hybrid and fully open access, and implements the data model in draft_implementation.md. hoaddata 0.3 stays available unchanged for code that relies on its tables.

  • The build runs as a targets pipeline (_targets.R): only steps whose inputs changed rerun (raw files, SQL templates, Crossref/OpenAlex snapshots, calendar year). GitHub Actions runs it on demand (build.yaml) and checks the package on every push (check.yaml). New helpers jn_bq_auth(), jn_snapshots() and jn_save_reference().

  • Agreement coverage: new reference table agreement_institutions (JCT institutions with ROR IDs), article-level article_agreements in BigQuery (matches by corresponding or first author, direct, child, parent or related institution per OpenAlex, with the OpenAlex publication date within the agreement period) and the aggregate agreement_journal_year (direct, child and parent matches; related ones are kept for comparison only). Agreements missing from ESAC get an inferred period (agreements.is_period_inferred).

  • pkgdown website with a README home page and a “Data model” article that documents every table, column and counting rule from the schema; deployed to GitHub Pages by pkgdown.yaml.

  • All tables, including the article tables, are published as Parquet files in the Hugging Face dataset najkoja/jn_analytics, one tagged commit per release (named after the build date), with a generated dataset card. New jn_upload_hf(); the pipeline exports and uploads after each build. The Parquet files are no longer committed to parquet/ of the repository. The website’s “Download the data” page links to Hugging Face.

  • jn_publish() exports all tables (see jn_publish_tables()); the article tables are written as one file per publication year (articles/articles_2025.parquet, …).

  • The article tables are partitioned by pub_year in BigQuery, so queries and exports for single years scan less. article_first_authors and article_agreements have a new pub_year column.

  • jn_source() reads tables stored as a folder of files, so the article tables can be analysed from a download as well as from BigQuery.

  • Two new tables for drill-downs by institution, for example in the dashboard: agreement_articles lists every eligible work per agreement, participating institution and author role with its journal, type and OA status (no joins needed), and agreement_institution_year sums it per institution, year, OA model and work type. agreement_articles is clustered by agreement and institution in BigQuery and sorted that way in its yearly Parquet files, so a query for one agreement reads little data.

  • Agreement coverage counts a parent match only if the agreement lists at least two institutions whose only parent it is (an umbrella organisation such as CSIC or the Chinese Academy of Sciences). Otherwise the match is stored as parent_single and not counted: OpenAlex lists the shareholders of European XFEL (CNRS, INFN, CEA and others) as its parents, and Spanish universities as parents of joint institutes with CSIC, which made their authors eligible under agreements that do not cover them. In 2025 this removes about 24,000 of 25,500 work-agreement pairs counted only through a parent.

  • Curated corrections of the JCT institution lists in data-raw/manual/institution_corrections.csv add or remove participating institutions per agreement, with their source. The first fixes ieee2025cas (IEEE and DRAA) against IEEE’s partner list: six universities added, among them South China University of Technology, and fourteen removed. A correction that no longer applies stops the build.

  • normalize_ror() brings ROR IDs into one canonical form.

  • A CC licence counts for the version of record whatever its start date in Crossref (delay_in_days is ignored), as in hoaddata 0.3.

  • Every work in a fully OA journal-year counts as OA (articles_oa); in hybrid journal-years, OA means a CC licence in Crossref. The licence evidence alone is the new articles_with_cc_license in journal_year, journal_year_country and agreement_journal_year, reported by jn_metadata() as share_cc_license.

  • All journal-year aggregates carry a year-aware oa_model: a journal counts as hybrid up to and including its OpenAlex oa_flip_year (a transition year) and as fully OA afterwards.

  • Publisher-wide flips to open access are curated in data-raw/manual/oa_flips.csv. ACM journals count as fully OA from 2026.

  • jn_oa(), jn_licenses() and jn_metadata() give journal-level statistics per agreement: by = "agreement_id" and agreement = <ESAC IDs> cover all works in an agreement’s journals, by default only in the years the agreement ran (agreement_period).

  • The analysis functions cover all journals by default; split hybrid from fully OA journals with by = "oa_model" or filter with oa_model.

  • The Journal Checker Tool is the only source of journals and agreements. German Open Access Monitor (OAM) agreements are no longer included.

  • journals gains oa_model to tell hybrid from fully open access journals. Journals that hoaddata 0.3 dropped as fully OA are now kept and flagged.

  • Dashboard pages (portfolios) move from hoaddash config.csv into the data, one row per page and agreement, so each page lists its ESAC IDs; its journals follow from agreement_journals.

  • Journals get ISSN-Ls, titles, OpenAlex IDs and their OA model (hybrid or full_oa, plus oa_flip_year) from OpenAlex.

  • Article and aggregate tables count works by OpenAlex work_type, so all works and research articles (article, review) come from the same tables.

  • jn_bq_config() and jn_sql() define and render the BigQuery build; inputs are the OpenAlex (openalex_walden) and Crossref (cr_instant) snapshots, output goes to subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics.

  • jn_oa(), jn_licenses() and jn_metadata() compute OA shares, licence mix and metadata coverage for all journals or a portfolio, globally or by first-author country. They run unchanged on the Parquet export and on BigQuery via jn_source(); jn_tbl() gives direct access to any table, including article-level data in BigQuery.

  • jn_build() builds all BigQuery tables in order: articles, article_first_authors, journal_year, journal_year_country, journal_year_license and journal_year_country_license. Country tables cover every first-author country (full counting) instead of a fixed Germany scope.

  • jn_publish() exports the reference tables and journal-level aggregates as zstd-compressed Parquet with column descriptions in the file metadata, plus a release table (jn_release()) with version and snapshot dates.

  • jn_build_table() builds a table in BigQuery from an inst/sql template and sets column descriptions from the schema; jn_upload_reference() uploads the reference tables. articles is the first table built this way.

  • jn_fetch_openalex_sources() downloads OpenAlex journal metadata for the JCT journals.

  • jn_schema(), jn_tables() and jn_validate() expose and enforce one schema for column names, types and descriptions (inst/schema/columns.csv). Package docs are generated from it.

  • jn_update_reference() builds the reference tables journals, journal_issns, agreements, agreement_journals and portfolios.
